label: Thomas Edwin Castello (fabricated)
narrative: THE NAME WAS CONFESSED AS AN INVENTION BY THE MAN WHO SAYS HE INVENTED IT. Thomas Edwin Castello is presented in the Dulce literature as a security technician who worked inside the alleged facility, stole a set of photographs and papers, and vanished with his family. In November 2015 Tal Levesque, who wrote under the name Jason Bishop III and who authored the two original Dulce Base articles, told the researcher Adam Gorightly by email: 'You still do not get it. TEC (Thomas Edwin Castello) is a creation. A MYTH.' He named his ingredients in the same message and described mailing a hundred large packets of supporting material to authors and lecturers who then folded it into their own talks, articles and books. That last sentence is the important one, because it describes the deliberate manufacture of the appearance of independent corroboration: the many later sources that agree about Castello agree because they were seeded from one envelope. This node is therefore not an absence-of-record node and should never be rebuilt as one. Absence of record is what a board writes when it has looked and found nothing; here the author has spoken. The separate checks that were made are consistent with the confession and add nothing to it: John Greenewald, publishing on 1 April 2016, states 'There is no evidence that I have found, that shows that Thomas Costello even exists', and demonstrates that the single most-circulated piece of physical evidence attached to the name, a photograph of bodies in a chamber, is a frame from the 2000 film The 6th Day. One point of honesty about the sourcing: the confession reaches this board at second hand. It was read as reproduced on Norio Hayakawa's site, quoting Gorightly's book, and neither the email nor the book was opened. That is why the confession claim is graded Tier 2 rather than Tier 1, and it is the single item in this cluster most worth upgrading. A further negative recorded by Hayakawa in 2016, that an 'alleged' retired Air Force colonel told him no such person was ever employed at Dulce, is anonymous, is bracketed in quotation marks by Hayakawa himself, and is carried at Tier 3 so that nobody later mistakes it for a check. No jurisdiction, employer of record, date of birth or date of death has ever been attached to the name, which means no records search is even formulable: the claim is built so as to be unfalsifiable by records, and only its author could ever have settled it.
